sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are run on the same finite interval \(\Lambda_n\), with a prespecified washout and a fixed-width interior buffer.
sampling_model.units: One realization of a stationary radius-\(r\) innovation network on \(\mathbb Z\), observed through \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzed on \(I_n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments \(D_i^{(1)}\) and \(D_i^{(2)}\) enter the same local exposure maps and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensities are known from the design. The statistic estimates only the two wave means \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^{(2)}\); it does not estimate \(m_i\) or fit a regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 show that zero asymptotic variance for a stationary finite-variance finite-dependent sequence is equivalent to a finite-dependent coboundary and yields an unnormalized endpoint-difference law.
The paper proves consistency and asymptotic normality for exposure-IPW estimators under approximate neighborhood interference and studies network-HAC inference for one randomized finite population.
The paper proves central limit and invariance principles for stationary fields represented as functions of independent innovations under short-range physical dependence.
The paper proves treatment-effect asymptotics under graphon-random interference and develops direct- and indirect-effect inference.

The preprint proves asymptotic normality and optimality for regression-adjusted average-direct-effect estimators under graphon interference and consistently estimates the linear estimator's asymptotic variance under a low-rank graphon condition.

body.tldr: Two independent assignment waves on one buffered F\o lner interval turn the latent Palm population covariance into an observable cross-wave IPW moment. The already-proved mean-centered statistic \(\widehat\Omega_n^{12}\) has uniform finite-sample concentration and attains an \(n^{-1/2}\) separation. The new result defines the statistical experiment generated only by the two score arrays and proves that this attainable order is minimax sharp there by an explicit common-support four-point submodel, product relative entropy, Pinsker's inequality, and the two-point testing inequality. A lag-\((2r+1)\) cross-wave statistic is also exactly unbiased and has a no-bias \(O(\{\log(1/\delta)/n\}^{1/2})\) threshold; the sample-mean-centered statistic remains the headline procedure.

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 exactly classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, while existing network-interference papers analyze effect or variance estimation from one randomization. They do not define or solve the minimax testing problem for whether the Palm population component vanishes under two repeated assignments. The sharpness question is meaningful only after fixing what the test observes.
project_justification.niche: Repeated randomization on the same local network makes cross-wave IPW products conditionally remove assignment noise. Restricting decisions to the sigma-field generated by the two score arrays yields a precise score-observation experiment in which a common-support four-point family can certify the information lower bound.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the score-measurable randomized-test class and its level-alpha, type-II-beta separation radius, combines the existing uniform \(O(n^{-1/2})\) achievable radius with an explicit matching Le Cam lower bound at \(p=1/2\), and therefore proves \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) score-experiment optimality. It also supplies an exactly unbiased lag-separated cross-wave diagnostic with an explicit bounded-differences threshold and no centering-bias term.

body.related_work: Janson2015 is the primary mathematical comparator. Its Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 give the finite-dependent zero-variance, block-factor coboundary, and endpoint-difference laws; those results remain cited substrate for interpreting the null and do not contain the present testing experiment. Leung2022ANI supplies the one-wave exposure-IPW framework and approximate-neighborhood-interference perspective, but its finite-population target and network-HAC analysis differ from the two-wave Palm population-variance diagnostic here. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings and known-propensity design foundations, not a repeated-wave population-covariance test. The root-sample-size upper guarantee was already established by the mean-centered cross-wave concentration theorem; the new contribution is its matching information lower bound for tests measurable only through the two score arrays. Tsybakov2009 supplies Pinsker's classical inequality, and McDiarmid1989 supplies the bounded-differences inequality used for the supporting exactly unbiased statistic. LiWager2022 studies direct and indirect effects under a generally dense graphon-random model, while FanLengWu2025 studies regression adjustment and low-rank-graphon variance estimation for the average direct effect; neither solves this score-experiment zero-boundary problem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied after a prespecified washout to the same no-carryover potential-outcome schedule. The matching lower bound is proved only for tests measurable with respect to the two exposure-IPW score arrays, and at the explicit Bernoulli submodel \(p=1/2\); tests using innovations, the graph, assignments, exposures, or outcomes beyond their score map are outside that converse. The single-wave BondEtAl2012 experiment therefore cannot be reanalyzed with this diagnostic without a second compatible assignment wave. The finite-radius and ambient-interval formulation remains deliberate: no graph-distance HAC, endogenous random-metric, random-radius stabilization, or unchanged-HAC claim is made.
body.honest_scope: The observable cross-wave identity, uniform concentration bound, and size--power theorem establish the attainable root-sample-size radius. The new theorem proves this rate is minimax sharp in the explicitly defined score-observation experiment when \(p=1/2\) and \(\alpha+\beta<1\); it does not claim a lower bound for a richer raw-data experiment or for arbitrary \(p\). The lag-separated statistic is a supporting exactly unbiased alternative with a no-bias threshold, while the sample-mean-centered statistic remains the headline. Janson's coboundary and endpoint law, Pinsker's inequality, and the bounded-differences inequality are published inputs and carry no novelty claim.
